title: Reinforcing L2 reading comprehension through artificial intelligence intervention: refining engagement to foster self-regulated learning
extended_summary:
This paper investigates whether an artificial-intelligence-supported reading environment can improve second-language (L2) reading comprehension, learner engagement, and self-regulated learning. The study addresses a gap in the literature on AI for reading instruction, especially for language learners, by asking whether AI-enhanced classrooms can outperform conventional instruction and how learners perceive such an environment.

The intervention centered on the ReadToMe (RTM) platform, an AI-based, multi-sensory reading system that converts curricular text into text-to-speech, synchronized highlighting, pronunciation support, concept images, dictionary support, and knowledge-graph-based scaffolds. In the experimental condition, students used RTM for homework and reading practice, while the control group received conventional reading instruction and feedback from the teacher or peers. The study used a mixed-methods design with pre/post quantitative measures and follow-up semi-structured interviews.

Participants were 60 Iranian female EFL students from two intact classes at a language institute, with 30 students in the experimental group and 30 in the control group. They were upper-intermediate/C1 learners with a mean age of 21, attending in-person classes twice weekly for about 12 weeks. Both groups used the same reading textbook, and the same instructor taught both groups to reduce teacher effects. Outcomes included an objective reading comprehension test plus self-report scales for engagement and self-regulation.

The main findings indicate that the AI-supported group significantly outperformed the control group on reading comprehension, self-regulation, and engagement. Qualitative data also suggested that most students viewed the AI platform as motivating, engaging, and helpful for personalized feedback and comprehension support, though some reported usability problems such as slow loading and navigation issues. Overall, the paper concludes that AI-enhanced reading instruction can be an effective approach for improving L2 reading outcomes and supporting learner engagement and self-regulated learning, while also noting the importance of addressing technical usability barriers.

identified_tools.name: ReadToMe
identified_tools.description: An AI-based reading and comprehension platform and intelligent learning companion that converts curriculum text into a proprietary multi-sensory format with text-to-speech, pronunciation localization, images, knowledge graphs, recording/analysis of oral reading, automated assessment, and remediation features.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the intervention platform in an AI-enhanced L2 reading classroom for upper-intermediate Iranian EFL learners to support homework and reading practice, with personalized feedback, text-to-speech, dictionary support, pronunciation practice, and comprehension scaffolds over a 12-week experiment.

findings.finding_summary: In a mixed-methods comparative experiment, the experimental group using ReadToMe outperformed the control group on post-instruction reading comprehension after controlling for pretest differences. ANCOVA showed a significant group effect on the reading test, F(1, 59)=43.82, p=0.000, partial η2=0.167; the total sample was n=60 (30 experimental, 30 control).
findings.measure: Reading comprehension test developed by Tong et al. (2017): 24 multiple-choice questions and 6 open-ended questions, maximum score 30

findings.finding_summary: ReadToMe produced significantly higher self-regulation outcomes than conventional instruction in the posttest when pretest scores were controlled. ANCOVA indicated a significant group effect for self-regulation, F(1, 59)=19.23, p=0.011, partial η2=0.151, with n=60 overall.

The ReadToMe intervention significantly improved learner engagement relative to the control condition after adjustment for pretest differences. ANCOVA found a significant group effect on engagement, F(1, 59)=24.11, p=0.000, partial η2=0.171, based on a total sample of 60 learners.
findings.measure: Revised School Engagement Scale (behavioral, cognitive, emotional engagement)

findings.finding_summary: Qualitative interview data indicated largely positive student perceptions of ReadToMe, with 77% of students highlighting the platform’s effectiveness in fostering engagement and supporting self-regulation, including themes such as increased attentiveness and enhanced motivation. However, 23% identified usability barriers, especially slow system responsiveness and interface/navigation issues, as limiting the platform’s effectiveness.
findings.measure: Semi-structured interview themes on engagement, motivation, self-regulation, and usability perceptions

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical mixed-methods pilot experiment with experimental and control groups and pre/post measurement, but it uses intact classes, a small sample (n=60), and does not establish a fully rigorous RCT. The evidence is stronger than descriptive work but still has design limitations typical of yellow-tier studies.
impact_tier_rationale: Reported effects were positive across reading comprehension, self-regulation, and engagement, with partial η2 values of 0.151 to 0.171, indicating modest positive impact by the framework provided here. Qualitative findings were also mostly favorable, though some usability issues reduced overall certainty.
